facts.fact: Josef Frank, after being the only Austrian to build a house at the 1927 Stuttgart Werkbund Estate, initiated the Vienna Werkbund Estate and was its artistic director.
facts.quote: After being the only Austrian to contribute a house to the Stuttgart Werkbund Estate in 1927, he became the initiator and artistic director of the Vienna Werkbund Estate.

facts.fact: Frank initiated and led the 1932 Werkbundsiedlung project in Vienna.
facts.quote: Frank was the initiator and leader of the 1932 project Werkbundsiedlung in Vienna.

facts.fact: Unlike most interwar Viennese architects, Frank favoured the settlement of small houses over the large municipal 'super blocks'.
facts.quote: Contrary to most other architects of the interwar period in Vienna, he took the idea of settlement and not the creation of so-called super blocks in the municipal housing.

facts.fact: The Stadio Flaminio is a stadium on the Via Flaminia, three kilometres northwest of central Rome.
facts.quote: The Stadio Flaminio is a stadium in Rome. It lies along the Via Flaminia, three kilometres northwest of the city centre, 300 metres away from the Parco di Villa Glori.

facts.fact: Inside the stands are a covered swimming pool and rooms for fencing, wrestling, weightlifting, boxing and gymnastics.
facts.quote: The interior spaces include a covered swimming pool, rooms for fencing, amateur wrestling, weightlifting, boxing, and gymnastics.

facts.fact: Pier Luigi Nervi designed it with his son, the architect Antonio Nervi, in 1957–58.
facts.quote: Pier Luigi Nervi designed the Flaminio Stadium with his son, the architect Antonio Nervi, between 1957 and 1958.

facts.fact: It was built for the 1960 Summer Olympics, opened in 1959, and hosted the Olympic football final.
facts.quote: The structure was built for the 1960 Summer Olympics and inaugurated in 1959. The Stadio Flaminio was built on the site of the previous Stadio Nazionale PNF. It was mostly devoted to football matches and served as the venue for the football final in the 1960 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: Abandoned for years, the stadium is in an advanced state of decay.
facts.quote: Abandoned for years, the stadium is now in an advanced state of decay.

facts.fact: In 2017 a Getty Foundation 'Keeping it Modern' grant paid for a conservation plan for the stadium.
facts.quote: In July 2017, with the cooperation of the Municipality of Rome, Sapienza University, Pier Luigi Nervi Project Association and DO.CO.MO.MO. Italy received a grant from the Getty Foundation and its Keeping it Modern program to prepare a conservation plan for the Stadio Flaminio.

facts.fact: It holds 32,000 people, 8,000 of them under cover.
facts.quote: With a capacity of 32,000 (8,000 covered), it was the smallest of the Six Nations stadiums.

facts.fact: The Lovell Health House is an International Style house designed and built by Richard Neutra in 1927–29 in Los Feliz, Los Angeles, for the physician and naturopath Philip Lovell.
facts.quote: The Lovell House or Lovell Health House is an  International style modernist residence designed and built by Richard Neutra between 1927 and 1929. The home, located at 4616 Dundee Drive in the Los Feliz neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, was built for the physician and naturopath Philip Lovell.

facts.fact: It is often called the first steel-frame house in the US and is an early use of gunite, sprayed-on concrete.
facts.quote: It is often described as the first steel frame house in the United States, and also an early example of the use of gunite (sprayed-on concrete).

facts.fact: Lovell's health ideas shaped the design: outdoor spaces for sunbathing, a rooftop solarium and rooms planned for maximum sunlight.
facts.quote: Known for his advocacy of natural living, Lovell emphasized the integration of health-focused features such as outdoor spaces for sunbathing, a rooftop solarium, and rooms designed to maximize UV exposure.

facts.fact: The frame uses open-web steel joists and four-inch-square steel posts five feet apart; the cantilevers that look freestanding are carried by the roof structure.
facts.quote: In its final form, the house incorporated innovative structural elements, such as open-web steel joists and four-inch-square steel posts spaced at five-foot intervals, emphasizing Neutra's mastery of steel construction techniques. While the steel cantilevers appear freestanding, they are supported by the roof structure.

facts.fact: The 4,800 sq ft, three-storey house was in MoMA's 1932 exhibition that defined the International Style.
facts.quote: The 4,800 sq ft (450 m2), three-story house aesthetically follows many of the principles of the International Style. It was included in the 1932 exhibit at the Museum of Modern Art in New York that retrospectively defined the style.

facts.fact: Its repeated factory-made window assemblies show Neutra's interest in industrial production.
facts.quote: In essence it reflects Neutra's interest in industrial production, and this is most evident in the repetitive use of factory-made window assemblies.

facts.fact: The porches and balconies hang down from the roof level.
facts.quote: The porches and balconies hung down from the roof level.

facts.fact: The entrance is on the top storey, through a terrace.
facts.quote: The entrance of the house is on the top story, through a terrace.

facts.fact: The Miller House and Garden in Columbus, Indiana, now a house museum, was designed by Eero Saarinen as a mid-century modern home for the businessman J. Irwin Miller and his wife Xenia.
facts.quote: The Miller House and Garden is a historic house museum at 2760 Highland Way in Columbus, Indiana, United States. It was designed by Eero Saarinen as a mid-century modern residence for the family of the businessman J. Irwin Miller and his wife Xenia Simons Miller.

facts.fact: Interior designer Alexander Girard, landscape architect Dan Kiley and Saarinen's associate Kevin Roche worked on parts of the design.
facts.quote: The interior designer Alexander Girard, the landscape architect Dan Kiley, and Saarinen's associate Kevin Roche assisted with various parts of the design.

facts.fact: Owned by the Indianapolis Museum of Art since 2009, the house and gardens are a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: The house and gardens, owned by the Indianapolis Museum of Art (IMA) since 2009, are designated as a National Historic Landmark.

facts.fact: It is a single-storey house on a terrace under a flat roof, 6,838 sq ft with six bedrooms; four zones branch off a central living room with a conversation pit.
facts.quote: The Miller House itself is a single-story house on a terrace, covered by a flat roof. It covers 6,838 square feet (635.3 m2) with six bedrooms. Inside, four zones branch off from a central living room that features a conversation pit.

facts.fact: The plan has nine bays marked by sixteen freestanding cruciform steel columns in a 4×4 grid that hold up the ceiling.
facts.quote: The floor plan is arranged into nine bays. The corners of the bays are delineated by sixteen freestanding, cruciform steel columns in a 4×4 arrangement, which support the ceiling.

facts.fact: A band of skylights runs unbroken around the edge of the roof's deep eaves.
facts.quote: The eaves are interspersed with a band of skylights, which continue uninterrupted along the perimeter of the house.

facts.fact: Kiley's garden is a modernist take on formal European gardens, inspired by the farmland patches he saw flying to Columbus.
facts.quote: Kiley's design was a modernist adaptation of formal European gardens, which are generally symmetrical and geometric, and was inspired by the patches of farmland he saw on his flights to Columbus.

facts.fact: The zones around a central space recall Palladio's Villa La Rotonda, but are arranged as a pinwheel.
facts.quote: The zones' arrangement is similar to Andrea Palladio's 16th-century Villa La Rotonda, where the rooms are also arranged around a central space, though the Miller House's zones are arranged in a pinwheel configuration.

facts.fact: Opened in 1954 at Fifth Avenue and 43rd Street, it was the first bank branch in the US built in the International Style.
facts.quote: Opened in 1954, it is the first bank branch in the United States to be built in the International Style.

facts.fact: Charles Evans Hughes III and Gordon Bunshaft of SOM designed it for the Manufacturers Trust Company.
facts.quote: Charles Evans Hughes III and Gordon Bunshaft of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) designed the building for the Manufacturers Trust Company.

facts.fact: Hughes won an internal SOM design competition with glass walls and a vault visible from outside; Bunshaft then revised his proposal.
facts.quote: Charles Evans Hughes III submitted the winning design, which featured glass walls and a bank vault visible from outside. Bunshaft was then tasked with revising Hughes's proposal.

facts.fact: The facade is mostly glass panes and aluminium mullions, and the vault door by Henry Dreyfuss can be seen from the street.
facts.quote: The facade is made largely of glass panes and aluminum mullions. The first story includes a door for the bank vault, designed by Henry Dreyfuss and visible from the street.

facts.fact: The second-floor glass panes were the largest ever made for a building at the time, each about 2.9 by 6.7 m.
facts.quote: The second-floor panes were the largest ever constructed for a building at that time, measuring 9+8⁄12 by 22 feet (2.9 by 6.7 m) and weighing 1,500 pounds (680 kg) each.

facts.fact: The concrete floor slabs cantilever out from the columns, with no supports at their edges, carried by steel and concrete beams.
facts.quote: The concrete floor slabs are cantilevered, extending outward from the columns without being supported at their edges, and are carried by steel and concrete beams.

facts.fact: Harry Bertoia's Golden Arbor, a screen of 800 brass, copper and nickel panels 70 feet long, stands on the second floor.
facts.quote: Adjoining the western wall is a floating sculptural screen of 800 intersecting brass, copper, and nickel panels, designed by Bertoia. Known as Golden Arbor, the screen is 70 feet (21 m) long and 16 feet (4.9 m) tall, weighing 5.25 short tons (4.69 long tons; 4.76 t).

facts.fact: New York City made the facade a landmark in 1997 and the interior in 2011.
facts.quote: The building's facade was designated as an official landmark by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) in 1997, and its interior was similarly designated in 2011.

facts.fact: The Oca is a white semi-sphere in Ibirapuera Park; together with the auditorium it forms a pair of pure white geometric volumes, considered the architecturally most important part of Niemeyer's project.
facts.quote: The group formed by the auditorium together with the Oca, which is a semi-sphere, composing two buildings of pure and white geometrical volumes, is considered the most important of the project from an architectural point of view.

facts.fact: Ibirapuera Park opened on 21 August 1954 for São Paulo's 400th anniversary.
facts.quote: It was inaugurated on 21 August 1954 for the 400th anniversary of the city of São Paulo with buildings designed by architect João Felipe Pereira and landscape by agronomist Otávio Augusto Teixeira Mendes.

facts.fact: In 2016 the park's complex of buildings by Oscar Niemeyer and others was listed as a national landmark by IPHAN.
facts.quote: In 2016, the complex of buildings designed by Oscar Niemeyer, alongside Zenon Lotufo, Hélio Uchôa Cavalcanti, and others, in the park were also registered as national landmark by the National Historic and Artistic Heritage Institute.

facts.fact: The Brasília TV Tower is a radio and television transmission tower opened in 1967, 224 metres tall, on the city's Monumental Axis.
facts.quote: The Brasília TV Tower (Portuguese: Torre de TV de Brasília) is a radio and television transmission tower built in Brasília and inaugurated in 1967 with a height of 224 meters.

facts.fact: Its base is a 25-metre triangular volume of exposed concrete enclosed in glass.
facts.quote: The base of the building is a triangular-shaped exposed concrete volume, twenty-five meters high, enclosed by glass.

facts.fact: Three pillars forming a V carry the volume and serve as the base for the metal tower.
facts.quote: The volume is supported by three pillars that form a V and enter the volume. The inner part of these pillars serve as a connection and base for the metallic tower, which starts from the volume where the Gems Museum is located.

facts.fact: The metal part is 192 metres high, in three sections.
facts.quote: The metallic part is one hundred and ninety-two meters high. It is composed of three sections, the first and longest one hundred and twenty-two meters, the second forty-five meters high, and the last twenty-four meters.

facts.fact: A viewing deck for 150 people sits 75 metres up, at the centre of the capital.
facts.quote: Taking advantage of its privileged location for observation, in the center of the capital, a belvedere was built at 75 meters high with capacity for 150 people.

facts.fact: It is the fourth tallest structure in Brazil.
facts.quote: The tower is the fourth tallest structure in Brazil and is also one of the most noticeable from Juscelino Kubitschek Bridge.

facts.fact: Morumbi is a 66,795-seat football stadium in São Paulo, home of São Paulo FC.
facts.quote: The Estádio Cícero Pompeu de Toledo, popularly known as Morumbi, and currently known as MorumBIS for sponsorship reasons, is a multipurpose 66,795-seater football stadium located in the eponymous district in São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.fact: It is the largest privately owned stadium in Brazil.
facts.quote: Morumbi is the largest privately owned stadium in Brazil.

facts.fact: Designed by João Batista Vilanova Artigas, it is a monument of Brazilian modernism, recognised by the city as a cultural building in 2018.
facts.quote: Designed by the architect João Batista Vilanova Artigas, the stadium is a monument of Brazilian modernism and in 2018 was formally marked as a cultural building by São Paulo city prefecture.

facts.fact: It opened part-built in 1960, with room for 70,000 people.
facts.quote: Eight years later, in 1960, the construction was partially concluded, and the stadium was inaugurated with a maximum capacity of 70,000 people.

facts.fact: When finished in 1970 it held 149,408 people; renovations later cut this to 66,795.
facts.quote: The Morumbi had a capacity of 149,408 people when completed in 1970. Its capacity was subsequently reduced through a series of renovations and changes to its permitted capacity, reaching 72,039 in 2006 and 66,795 in 2012.

facts.fact: Its attendance record is 138,032, set in 1977.
facts.quote: The stadium's attendance record currently stands at 138,032 people, set in 1977 when Ponte Preta was defeated by Corinthians 2–1.

facts.fact: The theatre was built between 1947 and 1950 to designs by Rino Levi, Roberto Cerqueira César and Fa Pestalozzi.
facts.quote: The construction of the theatre, between the years 1947 and 1950, was a period of enormous enthusiasm. The theatre was designed by leading architects Rino Levi, Roberto Cerqueira César and Fa Pestalozzi.

facts.fact: It opened on 8 and 9 March 1950 with concerts led by Heitor Villa-Lobos and Camargo Guarnieri.
facts.quote: The inauguration was on 8 and 9 March 1950, and was headed by two of the most important Brazilian conductors and composers. Heitor Villa-Lobos and Camargo Guarnieri led the concerts which also opened that year's season of concerts, conducting the São Paulo Symphony Orchestra and presenting their own musical creations.

facts.fact: It has two concert halls stacked one above the other, with 1,156 and 339 seats.
facts.quote: The theatre has two superposed concert halls, the first one named Sala Esther Mesquita, with 1156 seats, and the second one named Sala Rubens Sverner, with 339 seats.

facts.fact: A fire on 17 August 2008 destroyed most of the theatre, but Di Cavalcanti's facade survived.
facts.quote: Esther Mesquita, the main stage, was totally destroyed. Di Cavalcanti's façade survived the incident.

facts.fact: Late in the 1930s Levi's practice turned to theatres, including the Teatro Cultura Artística.
facts.quote: Towards the end of the decade, Levi's practice shifted to the design of theaters, including the Cine Ufa Palace and Teatro Cultura Artistic.

facts.fact: Lúcio Costa placed the bus station (Rodoviária) at the crossing of Brasília's Monumental and Residential axes, in the city centre.
facts.quote: At the intersection of the Monumental and Residential Axis, Costa planned the city center with the transportation center (Rodoviaria), the banking sector and the hotel sector.

facts.fact: Niemeyer's list of works gives the Ministry of Justice, or Palácio da Justiça, as a 1962 design.
facts.quote: 1962 – Ministério da Justiça or "Palácio da Justiça" (Ministry of Justice).

facts.fact: Torre Insignia, also called Torre Banobras, was designed by Mario Pani in the Tlatelolco housing complex in Mexico City.
facts.quote: Torre Insignia (also called Torre Banobras and the Nonoalco Tlatelolco Tower) is a building designed by Mario Pani Darqui located on the corner of Avenida Ricardo Flores Magón and Avenida de los Insurgentes Norte, in the Tlatelolco housing complex in Cuauhtémoc in Mexico City.

facts.fact: When finished in 1962 it was the second tallest building in Mexico, after the Torre Latinoamericana.
facts.quote: At its completion in 1962, the tower became the second tallest building in Mexico after the Torre Latinoamericana.

facts.fact: It is a triangular prism with a reinforced-concrete frame, and holds one of the tallest carillons in the world, with 47 bells by Petit & Fritsen.
facts.quote: The building has a triangular prism shape and was built with a reinforced concrete frame. It has been remodeled at least twice and houses one of the tallest carillon in the world, with 47 bells made by Petit & Fritsen.

facts.fact: It is 127 m tall with 25 floors.
facts.quote: Its height is 127 m (417 ft) and it has 25 floors

facts.fact: The carillon at the top was a gift from the Belgian government to Mexico City.
facts.quote: A carillon is installed in the building's highest point, which was a gift from the Belgian government to Mexico City.

facts.fact: It housed the state bank Banobras until the 1985 earthquake, then stood empty until 2011.
facts.quote: It was headquarters of the government bank Banobras until the 1985 Mexico City earthquake, when it was abandoned. It stood empty until 2011, when office space in the building was leased out to other companies.

facts.fact: It was built of reinforced concrete, glass and aluminium.
facts.quote: The construction materials used were reinforced concrete, glass, and aluminum.

facts.fact: The Plaza Cubierta is an indoor-outdoor 'open museum' that merges art with architecture and links many buildings of the campus's Central Complex.
facts.quote: The Plaza Cubierta is an indoor-outdoor space designed as an "open museum", combining art into the environment and architecture into art, and is considered one of the most important artistic and cultural works of the country. It also connects many different buildings in the Central Complex.:356-358

facts.fact: Villanueva meant it to be the heart of the campus, inspired by European halls and city plazas; it opened with the Aula Magna on 2 March 1954.
facts.quote: Villanueva wanted the Plaza Cubierta to be the heart of the campus, the physical and cultural center, being inspired by halls and city center plazas in Europe. It was inaugurated with the attached Aula Magna on 2 March 1954.:359

facts.fact: It joins the main library, rectory, students' union, Aula Magna, Paraninfo and concert hall.
facts.quote: Buildings connected by the Plaza Cubierta include: the main library, the rectory offices, the Federation of Students Center (students' union), the Aula Magna, the Paraninfo, and the concert hall (Sala de Conciertos).

facts.fact: Perforated walls, gaps in the roof and linking ramps give the space a sense of flow.
facts.quote: The Plaza Cubierta is noted for having perforated walls, sections of open roof, and a series of ramps linking elements, giving it a feeling of flow.

facts.fact: The campus became a World Heritage Site in 2000; UNESCO names the Covered Plaza among its masterpieces of modern architecture and visual art.
facts.quote: UNESCO describes it specifically as "an outstanding example of the Modern Movement in architecture" and adds that "[t]he university campus integrates the large number of buildings and functions into a clearly articulated ensemble, including masterpieces of modern architecture and visual arts, such as the Aula Magna with the "Clouds" of Alexander Calder, the Olympic Stadium, and the Covered Plaza."

facts.fact: The guiding idea of Villanueva's career was the 'synthesis of the arts'.
facts.quote: It was also during this time that he met the sculptor Francisco Narváez with whom he collaborated in the Museum of Fine Arts as well as in a series of other important projects like the "Natural Science Museum" (1936–1939) and the "Gran Colombia School" (1939–1942) which became Villanueva's first attempt to bring into fruition the guiding principle of career: the synthesis of the arts.

facts.fact: Parque Central is a housing, commercial and cultural development in El Conde, central Caracas.
facts.quote: The Parque Central Complex is a housing, commercial and cultural development, implemented by Centro Simón Bolívar and located in El Conde in the center of the city of Caracas, Venezuela adjacent to Paseo Vargas.

facts.fact: Its eight residential towers, started in 1970 and finished in 1972, each have 317 flats and stand 127 m and 44 storeys tall.
facts.quote: All eight buildings were residential with 317 apartments each, and each building was 127 meters and 44-storeys tall. These buildings were finished in 1972, while two commercial and office towers, known as Central Park Towers, were constructed between 1970 and 1983.

facts.fact: The complex also holds the Museum of Contemporary Art of Caracas, a children's museum, conference rooms, cinemas, a swimming academy and a heliport.
facts.quote: The Central Park complex also houses the Museo de Arte Contemporaneo de Caracas, The Children's Museum of Caracas, The Plenary Hall, 8 conference rooms, a swimming academy, movie theaters, a heliport and a parish center, among others.

facts.fact: The two 225 m, 59-storey office towers were the tallest in South America from 1979 until the Gran Torre Costanera in Santiago.
facts.quote: The Twin Towers of Central Park or Central Park Towers are a pair of 225 m tall skyscrapers. Between the completion of the west tower in 1979 and the completion of Gran Torre Costanera in Santiago (topped out in 2012), the 59-storey skyscrapers were the tallest in South America.

facts.fact: They were also the tallest in Latin America until 2003.
facts.quote: Until 2003, they were also the tallest in Latin America until surpassed by less than 1 meter by Torre Mayor in Mexico City.

facts.fact: A fire in October 2004 damaged the East Tower from the 34th to the 50th floor.
facts.quote: Just before midnight, October 17, 2004, a fire broke out in the East Tower, which housed government offices. The fire affected regions from the 34th floor to the 50th floor.

facts.fact: Estadio Centenario is Montevideo's football stadium, named after the centenary of Uruguay's constitution and owned by the Montevideo Department.
facts.quote: The Estadio Centenario (Spanish pronunciation: [estaðjo sentenaɾjo]; lit. 'Centenary Stadium', named after the centenary of Uruguay's Constitution) is an association football stadium in Montevideo, Uruguay. Located in the Parque Batlle neighbourhood, it is owned by the Montevideo Department.

facts.fact: It was built in 1929–30 to host the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.
facts.quote: The stadium was built between 1929 and 1930 to host the inaugural 1930 FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: In 1983 FIFA declared it the first Historical Monument of World Football, still the only building with that title.
facts.quote: On 18 July 1983, it was declared by FIFA as the first Historical Monument of World Football, to this day the only building to achieve this recognition worldwide.

facts.fact: Immigrant workers built it in a record nine months.
facts.quote: It was built especially for the 1930 FIFA World Cup, by immigrant workers in a record time of nine months.

facts.fact: It hosted the first World Cup final, which Uruguay won 4–2 against Argentina.
facts.quote: The final match of the inaugural World Cup matched Uruguay and Argentina, with Uruguay winning 4–2.

facts.fact: It has four grandstands separated by four lanes.
facts.quote: The stadium has four grandstands separated by four lanes.

facts.fact: The Uruguayan Football Museum sits under the Olympic stand; a 2004 remodelling added a panoramic lift to the Tower of Homage.
facts.quote: In 2004, it underwent a remodeling, in which a panoramic elevator was added to the Torre de los Homenajes.The Museum has a large collection of objects that are reminders of the most outstanding moments of Uruguayan and world football.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Public Works Building, now the Ministry of Health, is a rationalist public building at 9 de Julio and Belgrano avenues in Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: The Ministry of Public Works Building (Spanish: Edificio del Ministerio de Obras Públicas), now known as the Ministry of Health Building (Spanish: Edificio del Ministerio de Salud) is a public building in the rationalist style located on the intersection of 9 de Julio Avenue and Belgrano Avenue, in the neighborhood of Monserrat, in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

facts.fact: Built from 1932 to 1935, it was designed by Alberto Blanco; the architect José Hortal had first suggested it to the Minister of Public Works.
facts.quote: Built from 1932 to 1935, the building was designed by Belgrano Alberto Blanco and originally housed the offices of the Ministry of Public Works, which gives it its first and most commonly used name. Its construction was originally suggested by the architect José Hortal to the then Minister of Public Works Manuel Alvarado.

facts.fact: The building is several years older than 9 de Julio Avenue as it is today.
facts.quote: The building actually preceded the construction of the 9 de Julio Avenue as it is known today by several years.

facts.fact: Large steel portraits of Eva Perón cover its north and south walls.
facts.quote: On both the north and south walls, there are large steel portraits of María Eva Duarte de Perón, better known as Evita Perón.

facts.fact: The Evita portraits were made by the Argentine artist Alejandro Marmo in 2011.
facts.quote: The installations were created by the Argentinian artist Alejandro Marmo (known mononymously as Marmo) in 2011.

facts.fact: Built for the 1964 New York World's Fair in Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, the pavilion was designed by Philip Johnson and Richard Foster, with Lev Zetlin as structural engineer.
facts.quote: Constructed for the 1964 New York World's Fair, it was designed by the architects Philip Johnson and Richard Foster, with Lev Zetlin as the structural engineer.

facts.fact: It has three concrete-and-steel structures: the Tent of Tomorrow, the observation towers and the Theaterama; it is on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: The pavilion consists of three reinforced concrete-and-steel structures: the Tent of Tomorrow, observation towers, and Theaterama. It is owned by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation (NYC Parks) and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The Tent of Tomorrow is an ellipse 250 by 350 feet with a cable suspension roof and a terrazzo road map of New York State on its floor.
facts.quote: The Tent of Tomorrow is an elliptical structure measuring 250 by 350 feet (76 by 107 m) across, with a cable suspension roof and a terrazzo highway map of New York state on its floor.

facts.fact: The tallest of the three observation towers is 226 feet high; the drum-shaped concrete Theaterama has housed the Queens Theatre since 1989.
facts.quote: There are three observation towers, the tallest of which is 226 feet (69 m) high. The Theaterama, a drum-shaped reinforced concrete structure, has housed the Queens Theatre performing arts center since 1989.

facts.fact: The towers were added because Governor Rockefeller wanted the pavilion to be the tallest structure at the fair.
facts.quote: Another change to the original plans was the addition of observation towers, since Rockefeller wanted the New York State Pavilion to be the tallest structure in the fair.

facts.fact: The suspension roof was built at ground level and jacked up to the top of the columns 2.5 feet at a time.
facts.quote: The suspension roof was raised to the top of the tent's columns at the end of October, using jacks that lifted the roof 2.5 feet (0.76 m) at a time.

facts.fact: After years of neglect the Tent of Tomorrow was repainted in 2014 and the structures have been rehabilitated since 2019.
facts.quote: Following years of preservation efforts, the Tent of Tomorrow was repainted in 2014, and the structures underwent rehabilitation starting in 2019.

facts.fact: No 1 Poultry is an office and retail building at the apex of Poultry and Queen Victoria Street, beside Bank junction in the City of London.
facts.quote: No 1 Poultry is a commercial building in the City of London, used for offices and retail. It occupies the apex where the eastern ends of Poultry and Queen Victoria Street meet at Mansion House Street, the western approach to Bank junction.

facts.fact: It was one of James Stirling's final designs (1988–98), completed after his death by Michael Wilford.
facts.quote: No 1 Poultry in London (1988–98), one of Stirling's final designs, was posthumously completed by Wilford.

facts.fact: It replaced a plan for a Seagram-like modernist tower by Mies van der Rohe, abandoned after a long planning dispute in the 1980s.
facts.quote: An alternative scheme, a modernist tower by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe in the manner of the Seagram Building in New York City, was abandoned after a high-profile architectural and planning dispute in the 1980s.

facts.fact: The postmodern exterior is clad in alternating bands of pink and yellow limestone, and the courtyard atrium shows Stirling's vivid colour.
facts.quote: The exterior is clad in alternating bands of pink and yellow limestone, with voussoirs framing the apex arch, while the courtyard atrium displays some of Stirling's characteristic use of vivid colour.

facts.fact: Bucklersbury Passage runs through the building, linking its courtyard to the streets on either side.
facts.quote: Bucklersbury Passage runs through the building, linking the courtyard to Poultry on the north and Queen Victoria Street on the south.

facts.fact: The turret has been likened to a submarine conning tower, and the glazed two-sided clock recalls the Palazzo delle Poste in Naples.
facts.quote: The turret above has been likened to a submarine conning tower, while the glazed, two-sided clock recalls the Art Deco Palazzo delle Poste in Naples.

facts.fact: Listed Grade II* in 2016, it was then the youngest building in England with that grade.
facts.quote: Building users, neighbours and architectural experts urged Historic England to recognise and protect the building, and it was listed at Grade II*, making it, at the time, the youngest building in England to receive that designation.

facts.fact: A rooftop restaurant has a terrace and formal garden with wide views over the City.
facts.quote: A restaurant occupies the rooftop, with a terrace and formal garden offering wide City views for diners and drinkers.

facts.fact: The Mondadori Palace in Segrate, outside Milan, was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and built in 1970–75 as the headquarters of the publisher Arnoldo Mondadori Editore.
facts.quote: Designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer, it was built between 1970 and 1975 to serve as the headquarters for Arnoldo Mondadori Editore, one of Italy's largest publishing companies.

facts.fact: Giorgio Mondadori commissioned it after visiting Niemeyer's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Brasília in 1965.
facts.quote: The commission for the Mondadori Palace came about after Giorgio Mondadori, then president of the publishing company, visited Niemeyer's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Brasilia in 1965 and was impressed by its design.

facts.fact: Engineer Bruno Contarini devised a suspension system to hang the glass box under the concrete arches.
facts.quote: The building was structurally engineered by Bruno Contarini, who came up with an innovative suspension system to support the cantilevered glass box under Niemeyer's distinctive concrete arches after the original engineering scheme proved unworkable.

facts.fact: The facade has bronze-tinted outer glass and clear inner glass with an air gap between to cut heat gain.
facts.quote: The curtain wall glass facade was made of bronze-tinted glass on the exterior and clear glass inside with an air cavity between to reduce heat gain.

facts.fact: It rises from an artificial lake by landscape architect Pietro Porcinai: a long five-storey glass office block under concrete arches, plus two smaller curved buildings.
facts.quote: The Mondadori Palace consists of three main elements emerging from an artificial lake designed by landscape architect Pietro Porcinai - a long five-story glass box containing the offices and newsrooms suspended under sweeping concrete arches, and two smaller curved ancillary structures with more organic shapes.

facts.fact: The 38 m by 200 m glass box hangs fully from the arches, floating 13 m above the water.
facts.quote: Rather than sitting directly on the ground, in the Mondadori Palace the 38m wide x 200m long glass box is fully suspended from the arches above, housing flexible open plan office space and floating 13m above the water. This produces a sense of lightness contrasting the solidity of the concrete.

facts.fact: Unlike the regular bays in Brasília, the arches follow an irregular, undulating rhythm.
facts.quote: The massive concrete arches have an irregular undulating rhythm unlike the regular modular bays in Brasilia.

facts.fact: The Stata Center, MIT's Building 32, is a 430,000 sq ft academic complex designed by Frank Gehry; it opened in March 2004.
facts.quote: The Stata Center, officially the Ray and Maria Stata Center and sometimes referred to as Building 32, is a 430,000-square-foot (40,000 m2) academic complex plus 290,000-square foot (27,000 m2) underground garage designed by architect Frank Gehry for the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). The building opened for initial occupancy on March 16, 2004.

facts.fact: It stands on the site of Building 20, the wartime 'temporary' building that housed the MIT Radiation Laboratory.
facts.quote: The Stata Center is located on the site of the former Building 20, demolished in 1998. Building 20 had been erected hastily during World War II as a temporary building to house the historic Radiation Laboratory.

facts.fact: Above the fourth floor the building splits into two towers, the Gates Tower and the Dreyfoos Tower.
facts.quote: Above the fourth floor, the building splits into two distinct structures: the Gates Tower and the Dreyfoos Tower, often called "G Tower" and "D Tower" respectively.

facts.fact: A wide ground-floor passage running the length of the building is called the Student Street.
facts.quote: A wide main passage running the length of the building on the ground floor is called the Charles M. Vest Student Street, in honor of the former MIT president who died in December 2013.

facts.fact: It houses computer science and AI labs (CSAIL), LIDS and the Department of Linguistics and Philosophy on its upper floors.
facts.quote: Research labs and offices of the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS), as well as the Department of Linguistics and Philosophy (Course 24) occupy the upper floors.

facts.fact: Critic Robert Campbell wrote that its tilting columns, colliding walls and changing materials (brick, mirror steel, aluminium, colour, corrugated metal) are a metaphor for the freedom and daring of the research inside.
facts.quote: Materials change wherever you look: brick, mirror-surface steel, brushed aluminum, brightly colored paint, corrugated metal. Everything looks improvised, as if thrown up at the last moment. That's the point. The Stata's appearance is a metaphor for the freedom, daring, and creativity of the research that's supposed to occur inside it."

facts.fact: In 2007 MIT sued Gehry and the builders over leaks, cracking masonry and mould; the suit was settled in 2010.
facts.quote: On October 31, 2007, MIT sued architect Frank Gehry and the construction companies, Skanska USA Building Inc. and NER Construction Management, for "providing deficient design services and drawings" which caused leaks to spring, masonry to crack, mold to grow, drainage to back up, and falling ice and debris to block emergency exits.

facts.fact: Aldo Rossi designed the complex in 1996 on a large Berlin corner block once crossed by a section of the Berlin Wall.
facts.quote: In 1996 Rossi designed a building complex on a large corner block in the Schützenquartier, Berlin, and previously occupied by a section of the Berlin Wall.

facts.fact: From his study of the city, Rossi made a single building that looks like many, with fronts of different widths, designs and colours, many drawing on the Italian palazzo.
facts.quote: Rossi's study of the architecture of the city led him to construct a single building with the appearance of multiple structures, of varying widths, designs and colours, many of which have elements of Palazzo architecture.

facts.fact: Rossi's list of works dates the Schützenstraße quarter to 1994–1998.
facts.quote: 1994–1998 Schützenstraße quarter, Berlin (photographs)

facts.fact: The Hill of the Buddha is a Buddhist shrine at Makomanai Takino Cemetery in Sapporo, designed by Tadao Ando.
facts.quote: The Hill of the Buddha (Japanese: 頭大仏, Hepburn: Atama Daibutsu; "Large Buddha's Head") is a Buddhist shrine at Makomanai Takino Cemetery (Japanese: 真駒内滝野霊園) in Sapporo, Japan, designed by Japanese modernist architect Tadao Ando.

facts.fact: A 13.5 m Buddha statue is ringed by an artificial hill planted with 150,000 lavender plants.
facts.quote: The shrine features a 13.5 m (44 ft) tall statue of the Buddha encircled by an artificial hill rotunda planted with 150,000 lavender plants.

facts.fact: The design wrapped an existing statue, carved around 2000, that had stood alone.
facts.quote: The design incorporated the pre-existing Buddha statue, which was sculpted circa 2000 and stood solitary.

facts.fact: From outside only the head shows above the hill; visitors enter through a tunnel to see the whole statue in the open rotunda.
facts.quote: On approaching the statue, only the head sticks out from the hill, and the shrine is entered through a tunnel for a full view of the statue inside of the open rotunda.

facts.fact: It opened in December 2015.
facts.quote: The building opened in December 2015.

facts.fact: Renzo Piano's Zentrum Paul Klee near Bern was built 1999–2005, one of a series of his art museums each very different from the others.
facts.quote: The Zentrum Paul Klee near Bern, Switzerland (1999–2005), continued his series of art museums each very different from the others.

facts.fact: It was designed largely to protect Paul Klee's fragile drawings from sunlight.
facts.quote: It was designed in large part to protect the fragile drawings of Paul Klee from sunlight.

facts.fact: Its galleries look like the rolling hills of the Swiss countryside.
facts.quote: It housed in a series galleries resembling rolling hills in the Swiss countryside.

facts.fact: Piano said the gallery shapes came from ships' hulls, shaped to waves as the building is shaped to the landscape.
facts.quote: Piano explained that the shape of the galleries was inspired by naval architecture and the hulls of ships, which were adapted to the form of waves as his building was adapted to the landscape.

facts.fact: Hong Kong International Airport opened in 1998; its passenger terminal was the largest in the world at the time.
facts.quote: Opened in 1998, Hong Kong International Airport is the world's busiest cargo gateway and one of the world's busiest passenger airports. It is also home to one of the world's largest passenger terminal buildings, which was the largest when the airport opened.

facts.fact: The airport at Chek Lap Kok replaced the crowded Kai Tak Airport, built in 1925.
facts.quote: Chek Lap Kok Airport was designed as a replacement for the Kai Tak Airport, built in 1925.

facts.fact: Foster and Partners were the terminal's architects, with Ove Arup designing the roof structure and Mott Connell leading the consortium.
facts.quote: The detailed design for the airport terminal was awarded to a consortium led by Mott Connell (the Hong Kong office of UK consultant Mott MacDonald) with BAA PLC as the specialist designers for airport-related aspects, Foster and Partners as the architects, and Ove Arup as the specialist structural designers for the roof.

facts.fact: The mostly glass sides were designed to break in high winds, relieving pressure so the terminal can survive a typhoon.
facts.quote: The sides of the terminals, predominantly glass, were designed to break during high-speed winds, relieving pressure and allowing the terminal to withstand an intense typhoon.

facts.fact: Terminal 1 covers 570,000 m², one of the largest passenger terminals in the world.
facts.quote: Terminal 1 (T1) of the HKIA, with an area measuring 570,000 square metres (6,100,000 sq ft), is one of the largest passenger airport terminal buildings in the world, after the likes of Dubai International Airport Terminal 3 and Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3.

facts.fact: Despite its size, the layout, signs, moving walkways and a driverless people mover were planned to make the terminal easy to use.
facts.quote: Despite its size, the passenger terminal was designed for convenience. The layout and signage, moving walkways and the automated people mover help passengers move through the building.

facts.fact: Construction of the airport began in 1991.
facts.quote: Construction of the new airport began in 1991.

facts.fact: Milstein Hall, designed by OMA's Rem Koolhaas and Shohei Shigematsu, is a cantilevered building of studio space that reaches out over University Avenue at Cornell.
facts.quote: Directly behind Sibley, the OMA/Rem Koolhaas and Shohei Shigematsu-designed Milstein Hall (named after Paul Milstein) is a prominent cantilevered structure housing studio space that extends over University Avenue.

facts.fact: The LEED-certified building has a stepped auditorium, crit space, galleries and a sunken garden.
facts.quote: The LEED-certified building features a stepped auditorium space for presentations and meetings, crit space, galleries, and a sunken garden.

facts.fact: It opened to students, still unfinished, in autumn 2011.
facts.quote: The unfinished building opened to students in the fall of 2011, with the ceremonial completion scheduled the following spring.

facts.fact: In 2013 it won an AIA Honor Award for architecture, one of 11 buildings in the US and Canada.
facts.quote: In 2013, Milstein Hall was one of 11 buildings in the United States and Canada to receive an Honor Award for architectural design from the American Institute of Architects.

facts.fact: The European Court of Human Rights building stands in Strasbourg's European Quarter; it was designed by the Richard Rogers Partnership with Claude Bucher and completed in 1994.
facts.quote: The building of the European Court of Human Rights is located in the European Quarter of Strasbourg, France. It was designed by the Richard Rogers Partnership and Claude Buche and was completed in 1994.

facts.fact: It sits on the corner where the river Ill meets the Marne–Rhine Canal.
facts.quote: The building is located on the eastern corner of the water intersection, where the Ill river is crossed by the Canal de la Marne au Rhin.

facts.fact: Designed in 1989, it was meant as 'a symbolic landmark but not a monument', welcoming and open rather than fortress-like.
facts.quote: They intended to create a "symbolic landmark but not a monument". They also, due to the nature of the court, wanted to make it more welcoming and open rather than fortress-like.

facts.fact: The design was stretched during planning when the fall of the Eastern Bloc raised the need for offices by 50%.
facts.quote: The original design was stretched as, during design, the demand for office space grew by 50% due to the fall of the Eastern Bloc.

facts.fact: It relies on natural light and ventilation, apart from the air-conditioned entrance hall.
facts.quote: The building relies on natural light and ventilation, except the light entrance hall which is air conditioned in an energy saving manner.

facts.fact: The court and commission occupy two large circular chambers, with offices in a 'tail' stretching behind.
facts.quote: The two main organs of the court, the court and commission, occupy two large circular chambers each side and offices are located in a "tail" stretching behind the building.

facts.fact: Built by 50 firms with 125 subcontractors, it cost 544 million French francs, paid by the Council of Europe's member states; the City of Strasbourg gave the site.
facts.quote: It was built by 50 firms with 125 subcontractors and cost 544 million French Francs, which came from the member states of the Council of Europe which owns the building, however the site it was built on was provided by the City of Strasbourg.

facts.fact: It has 28,000 m² of floor space; the courtroom covers 860 m² with 260 seats.
facts.quote: The building has 28,000 square metres of floor space. The Court Room covers 860 square metres and has 260 seats, with an extra 49 for judges and 33 for applicants (the deliberation room has 47 places with an additional 52 seats).

facts.fact: The KKL in Lucerne, designed by Jean Nouvel, combines a concert hall, an art museum, conference rooms and restaurants.
facts.quote: Designed by French architect Jean Nouvel, the complex includes a concert hall, an art museum, conference facilities, and restaurants.

facts.fact: The concert hall opened on 18 August 1998 and the whole complex in March 2000.
facts.quote: The concert hall opened on 18 August 1998, and the full complex was inaugurated in March 2000.

facts.fact: It has a roof 100 by 100 metres and was designed with special care for acoustics.
facts.quote: The structure features a roof measuring 100 by 100 metres and was designed with particular attention to acoustics.

facts.fact: It is the main venue of the annual Lucerne Festival.
facts.quote: The Centre regularly hosts cultural events and serves as the central venue for the annual Lucerne Festival.

facts.fact: It stands beside the lake in the city centre, and its concert hall, with acoustics by Russell Johnson, is one of the world's leading halls.
facts.quote: The Culture and Convention Center (KKL) beside the lake in the center of the city was designed by Jean Nouvel. The center has one of the world's leading concert halls, with acoustics by Russell Johnson.

facts.fact: It houses the Museum of Art Lucerne (Kunstmuseum Luzern).
facts.quote: KKL houses a concert hall as well as the Museum of Art Lucerne (Kunstmuseum Luzern).

facts.fact: Nara Centennial Hall is a multi-use complex that opened in 1999 for the centenary of the municipality of Nara.
facts.quote: Nara Centennial Hall (なら100年会館, Nara Hyakunen Kaikan) is a multi-use complex in Nara, Japan. It opened in 1999 as part of the centennial celebrations of the  municipality of Nara.

facts.fact: It has a large hall for up to 1,720 people, a 446-seat concert hall and a gallery.
facts.quote: There is a large hall that seats up to 1720, a smaller concert hall with a capacity of 446, and a gallery.

facts.fact: Arata Isozaki was the architect, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.
facts.quote: Arata Isozaki was the architect, with acoustical design by Nagata Acoustics.

facts.fact: Opera Village Africa is an arts education project in Burkina Faso, started by the German director and artist Christoph Schlingensief.
facts.quote: Opera Village Africa (French: Village-Opéra Afrique, German: Operndorf Afrika) is an arts education project located in Ouagadougou, the capital city of Burkina Faso. It was initiated by the German film and theatre director, actor, and artist, Christoph Schlingensief.

facts.fact: In 2008 Schlingensief brought in the Burkinabè architect Diébédo Francis Kéré.
facts.quote: To realise the project, in the year 2008 Christoph Schlingensief brought on board architect and development activist Diébédo Francis Kéré, who was born in Burkina Faso.

facts.fact: Kéré combines a traditional way of building with ecological ideas and sustainable materials.
facts.quote: Kéré brings together a traditional building style with ecological and sustainable concepts using sustainable materials.

facts.fact: Local people, trained in construction, put up the buildings, and Kéré's own materials keep them cool.
facts.quote: The buildings are built by the local population who have undergone construction training. Here, Kéré also places value on air conditioning, achieving cooling by using his specially developed construction materials.

facts.fact: In 2011 sixteen buildings opened, including a primary school that takes 50 new pupils a year.
facts.quote: 2011 saw the opening of 16 buildings including the primary school, which takes on 50 new pupils every year.

facts.fact: A hospital with primary care, maternity and dental units was started in 2012 and opened in 2014.
facts.quote: In April 2012, building work began on the hospital consisting of a primary medical care unit, a maternity ward and a dental care unit. It was opened in 2014.

facts.fact: A 'Festspielhaus' for cultural encounters is planned at the centre of the grounds as the heart of the project.
facts.quote: The "Festspielhaus" – a place of cultural encounter – at the centre of the grounds is planned to form the heart of the project.

facts.fact: Riken Yamamoto's list of selected works gives The Circle at Zürich Airport as 2018.
facts.quote: 2018: The Circle at Zürich Airport

facts.fact: Its architect, Riken Yamamoto, won the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2024.
facts.quote: In 2024, Yamamoto was awarded the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

facts.fact: Morphosis's Emerson College Los Angeles Center was completed in 2014.
facts.quote: Emerson College Los Angeles Center, Los Angeles, California, 2014

facts.fact: The Emerson College Los Angeles campus won nine awards for Morphosis.
facts.quote: Morphosis has been recognized with more than 190 local, national and international awards, including nine for the design of the Emerson College Los Angeles campus and 16 for the Perot Museum of Nature and Science.

facts.fact: Among them was the 2014 Los Angeles Architecture Awards Grand Prize for the Hollywood campus.
facts.quote: These include the 2014 Los Angeles Architecture Awards Grand Prize, presented by the Los Angeles Business Council, for designing the campus of Emerson College in Hollywood.

facts.fact: Vulcania, the 'European Park of Volcanism', is an educational volcano-themed park and museum at Saint-Ours-les-Roches, 15 km from Clermont-Ferrand, opened in 2002.
facts.quote: Vulcania, the "European Park of Volcanism", is an educational French amusement park and museum with a volcano theme. Situated in Saint-Ours-les-Roches, Auvergne, 15 km north-west of Clermont-Ferrand, it was officially inaugurated in 2002.

facts.fact: The idea came from the volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft, who died at Mount Unzen in 1991.
facts.quote: The project was the brainchild of French volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft, who died at Mount Unzen in 1991.

facts.fact: Hans Hollein's ideas for an underground museum, first drawn for an unbuilt Guggenheim in Salzburg, were realised at Vulcania (1997–2002).
facts.quote: The later hasn't been built, but his ideas for an underground museum still materialised in the Vulcania European Centre of Vulcanology in Auvergne in France (1997–2002).

facts.fact: Three-quarters of the foundations are sunk underground.
facts.quote: Three-quarters of the foundations are sunk underground, which aided in the rehabilitation of the land.

facts.fact: Visitors walk down a ramp towards a 'metaphorical volcano': a cone clad in dark stone and lined inside with gold metal.
facts.quote: Visitors approach a 'metaphorical Volcano' by descending down a ramp towards a cone-shaped structure clad in dark stone and lined on the inside with a gold metal.

facts.fact: It includes research and conference rooms, IMAX theatres, greenhouses showing volcanic fertility and a restaurant overlooking the nature park.
facts.quote: The design incorporates research and conference facilities, large IMAX theaters, greenhouses to highlight the positive effects of volcanism — fertility — and a restaurant with views out to the whole nature park.

facts.fact: Building it in the heart of the Chaîne des Puys met strong opposition from conservationists.
facts.quote: From an environmental perspective, the construction of Vulcania in the heart of the Chaîne des Puys met strong opposition from conservationists.

facts.fact: Preston bus station is the city's central bus station, a Brutalist building of 1968–69 designed by Keith Ingham and Charles Wilson of Building Design Partnership with E. H. Stazicker, engineered by Ove Arup & Partners.
facts.quote: It was designed by Ove Arup & Partners in Brutalist architectural style between 1968 and 1969, to a design by Keith Ingham and Charles Wilson of Building Design Partnership with E. H. Stazicker. It was built by John Laing.

facts.fact: Until 2017 it held 80 double-decker buses, 40 along each side.
facts.quote: Built in Brutalist architectural style between 1968 and 1969, designed by Keith Ingham and Charles Wilson of Building Design Partnership with E. H. Stazicker, it had (until 2017) a capacity of 80 double-decker buses, 40 along each side of the building.

facts.fact: Above the bus deck is a five-floor car park for 1,100 cars.
facts.quote: Pedestrian access to the bus station was originally through any of three subways, one of which linked directly to the adjacent Guild Hall, while the design also incorporates a multi-storey car park of five floors with space for 1,100 cars.

facts.fact: The Twentieth Century Society calls it one of the most significant Brutalist buildings in the UK.
facts.quote: It has been described by the Twentieth Century Society as "one of the most significant Brutalist buildings in the UK".

facts.fact: Arup's engineers curved the car-park balconies because finishing a vertical wall was too costly; the curves also protect car bumpers.
facts.quote: The building's engineers, Ove Arup & Partners, designed the distinctive curve of the car park balconies "after acceptable finishes to a vertical wall proved too expensive, contributing to the organic, sculptural nature of the building. The edges are functional, too, in that they protect car bumpers from crashing against a vertical wall.

facts.fact: Threatened with demolition in the 2000s, it was listed Grade II in September 2013 after two failed attempts, then refurbished and reopened in July 2018.
facts.quote: After two unsuccessful attempts, it was granted Grade II listed building status in September 2013. It was then refurbished and reopened in July 2018.

facts.fact: John Puttick Associates won the 2015 RIBA competition for its renovation, with Cassidy + Ashton as partner.
facts.quote: In August 2015, New York-based (with offices in London) architecture company John Puttick Associates' entry was chosen as the winning design.

facts.fact: The refurbishment won a RIBA National Award and was long-listed for the 2019 Stirling Prize.
facts.quote: As a regional winner, the bus station was also a nominee for and won a RIBA National Award and received long-listing for the 2019 RIBA Stirling Prize but did not make the short list.

facts.fact: Ove Arup personally supervised the design and construction of Kingsgate Bridge in Durham in 1963.
facts.quote: Ove Arup personally supervised the design and construction of Durham's Kingsgate Bridge in 1963.

facts.fact: It was the firm's first bridge, Arup was particularly attached to it, and his ashes were scattered from it.
facts.quote: As the firm's first bridge project, Arup held a particular attachment to it, and after his death, his ashes were scattered from the bridge.

facts.fact: A bust of Arup stands at one end of the bridge; it was stolen in 2006 and replaced.
facts.quote: A bust of Arup, placed at one end of the bridge, was stolen in the summer of 2006 but has since been replaced.

facts.fact: It was the last structure designed by Arup himself.
facts.quote: Kingsgate Bridge was the last structure designed by Arup.

facts.fact: The Media-TIC building by Enric Ruiz-Geli (Cloud 9) is one of the notable buildings of Barcelona's Poblenou district.
facts.quote: Major public spaces include the Parc de Diagonal Mar (Enric Miralles), the Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, the Parc Central del Poblenou (Jean Nouvel), the beachfront Parc del Poblenou, the vast Parc del Forum, Oficines Diagonal 197 (David Chipperfield), the Media-Tic Building (Enric Ruiz Geli - CLOUD 9), the historic Poblenou Cemetery as well as many kilometres of beaches.

facts.fact: The LocHal public library in Tilburg reuses a redundant steel locomotive shed, designed to spark many kinds of interaction between people.
facts.quote: For example, the LocHal Public Library located in the Dutch city of Tilburg was designed by a collective of architects, Mecanoo, who sought to repurpose a redundant steel locomotive shed with a view to activating multifaceted interactions between people in a physical space.

facts.fact: This aim of creating social interaction leads it to be classed as a 'social condenser'.
facts.quote: It is this desire to activate social interaction that leads to its classification as a Social Condenser.

facts.fact: It was named World Building of the Year at the 2019 World Architecture Festival in Amsterdam.
facts.quote: At the 2019 World Architecture Festival in Amsterdam, the LocHal Public Library was named ‘World Building of the Year’.

facts.fact: Behnisch Architekten completed Unilever's headquarters for Germany, Austria and Switzerland in Hamburg in 2009.
facts.quote: 2009 Unilever Headquarters Germany, Austria and Switzerland, Hamburg, Germany

facts.fact: Quay Quarter Tower in Sydney began as the AMP Centre of 1976 and was redeveloped from 2018 to 2021, gaining height, cantilevers and office space; it reopened in 2022 at 216 m with 54 floors.
facts.quote: Built as the AMP Centre in 1976, the structure underwent a redevelopment from 2018 to 2021, which increased its height, introduced cantilevers, created additional office space, and modernised the tower's overall form and design. The AMP Centre re-opened as Quay Quarter Tower in early 2022, and stands at a height of 216 metres (709 ft) with 54 floors.

facts.fact: It is the world's first 'upcycled' skyscraper, keeping 68% of the old building's structure, and was World Building of the Year at the 15th World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: It is the world's first upcycled skyscraper retaining 68% of the existing building's structure and named World Building of the Year at the 15th annual World Architecture Festival.

facts.fact: 3XN's design won a competition run by BVN, which then became executive architect and developed it with 3XN.
facts.quote: On 24 September 2014, the winning design from architect 3XN was revealed and BVN was appointed Executive Architect to collaborate with 3XN and develop their design concept for construction.

facts.fact: The old core, 66% of the columns, beams and slabs and 95% of the internal walls were kept.
facts.quote: The AMP Centre's internal core, along with 66% of its existing columns, beams and slabs and 95% of its internal walls, were retained as part of the redevelopment.

facts.fact: The northern half was taken down and rebuilt around the existing core, and the southern half was reclad to match.
facts.quote: Following this, a new northern section for the structure was gradually built, incorporating it with the existing core and the southern section of the building, which was also reclad in a corresponding new façade.

facts.fact: The rebuilt tower has twice the floor space of the original, with a new cantilevered exterior.
facts.quote: The redevelopment resulted in a new height of 216 m (709 ft) with 54 floors, a completely new interior layout with twice the amount of total floorspace, and a new cantilevered exterior design.

facts.fact: In 2023 it received the CTBUH award for the world's best new tall building.
facts.quote: In 2023 the tower received the award for the world's best new tall building from the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH).

facts.fact: Behnisch Architekten, with Pohl Architekten, completed the Max Aicher Arena speed-skating stadium in Inzell in 2011.
facts.quote: 2011 Speed Skating Stadium Inzell – Max Aicher Arena (with Pohl Architekten), Inzell, Germany

facts.fact: Kurilpa Bridge is a pedestrian and cycle bridge over the Brisbane River, linking South Brisbane to the city centre; it was World Transport Building of the Year at the 2011 World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: The bridge connects Kurilpa Point in South Brisbane to Tank Street in the Brisbane central business district. In 2011, the bridge was judged World Transport Building of the Year at the World Architecture Festival.

facts.fact: Baulderstone built it, with Cox Rayner Architects and Arup Engineers in its design team.
facts.quote: Baulderstone built the bridge and the company's design team included Cox Rayner Architects and Arup Engineers.

facts.fact: It is the world's largest hybrid tensegrity bridge.
facts.quote: Kurilpa Bridge is the world's largest hybrid tensegrity bridge.

facts.fact: It is a multi-mast cable-stay structure that balances tension and compression to be light yet very strong.
facts.quote: The Kurilpa Bridge is a multiple-mast, cable-stay structure based on principles of tensegrity producing a synergy between balanced tension and compression components to create a light structure which is incredibly strong.

facts.fact: It is 470 m long with a 128 m main span, viewing platforms and an all-weather canopy along its full length.
facts.quote: The bridge is 470 metres (1,540 ft) long with a main span of 128 metres (420 ft) and features two large viewing and relaxation platforms, two rest areas, and a continuous all-weather canopy for the entire length of the bridge.

facts.fact: The structure has 18 steel deck sections, 20 steel masts and 16 horizontal spars.
facts.quote: The bridge structure comprises 18 structural steel bridge decks, 20 structural steel masts and 16 horizontal spars  or in layman's terms horizontal masts.

facts.fact: Its programmable LED lighting draws 75–100% of its power from solar energy.
facts.quote: Depending on lighting configurations, 75%-100% of the power required is provided by solar energy.

facts.fact: Its name is the Aboriginal word for the South Brisbane and West End area, meaning 'place for water rats'.
facts.quote: The name reflects the Australian Aboriginal word for the South Brisbane and West End area, and means 'place for water rats'.

facts.fact: The Surat Diamond Bourse, a diamond trading centre designed by Morphogenesis, is the world's largest office building, with 660,000 m² of floor space.
facts.quote: Surat Diamond Bourse (SDB) is a diamond trade centre located in DREAM City in Surat, Gujarat, India, designed by the architecture firm Morphogenesis. It is the world's largest office building with a floor space of 660,000 square metres (7,100,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: In August 2023 Guinness World Records declared it the world's largest office building, ahead of the Pentagon.
facts.quote: It was officially declared as the world's largest office building, surpassing The Pentagon, by the Guinness World Records on 22 August 2023.

facts.fact: It is made of nine linked 15-storey towers holding 4,200 offices.
facts.quote: The bourse comprises nine interconnected towers, each with 15 floors, accommodating 4,200 offices ranging from 28 square metres (300 square feet) to 700 square metres (7,500 square feet), out of which 2,700 offices are with 28 square metres (300 sq ft) area each in five towers, 900 offices with 46 square metres (500 sq ft) area in one tower, 400 offices with 93 square metres (1,000 sq ft) area in another tower, and two towers offering 350 larger offices exceeding 93 square metres (1,000 sq ft) area.

facts.fact: A central corridor joins the towers, like an airport terminal, with nine green 'Panchtattva' courts between the buildings.
facts.quote: The nine towers are connected with each other by a central corridor, with access to services and facilities similar to an airport terminal. There are nine Panchtattva courts in between the nine buildings, created as recreational and green spaces.

facts.fact: It has one of the world's largest radiant cooling systems.
facts.quote: It features one of the world’s largest radiant cooling systems.

facts.fact: The central spine flares into vertical fins that funnel gentle winds by the Venturi effect, while staggered atria let hot air escape by the stack effect.
facts.quote: The central spine flares into vertical fins to funnel low-intensity winds using the Venturi effect, while staggered atria allow for the escape of hot air through the stack effect, thereby maintaining a pleasant microclimate, or interior temperature.

facts.fact: Natural lighting halves its energy use, earning an IGBC Platinum rating.
facts.quote: The building consumes 50% less energy by using natural lighting systems, achieving a remarkable 45 kWh/sq.m./yr compared to the industry green benchmarks of 110 kWh/sq.m./yr. as per Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC), thus earning it the prestigious Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) Platinum rating.

facts.fact: Traders have been lukewarm about it because it sits on the city's outskirts with poor connections.
facts.quote: The bourse has received a lukewarm reception from diamond traders, as it is located on the outskirts of the city of Surat and has poor connectivity, when compared with the existing Bharat Diamond Bourse, located in the better-connected city of Mumbai.

facts.fact: The Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies building, known as the Minaretein, holds Education City's national mosque, teaching and faculty space and a research centre.
facts.quote: The mosque forms part of Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies (QFIS), located in the Minaretein building, on the campus of the Hamad Bin Khalifa University. Also included in the building is teaching and faculty space and a research centre for the QFIS.

facts.fact: Designed by Mangera Yvars and completed in 2013, it rests on five large columns standing for the five pillars of Islam, each bearing a verse of the Qur'an.
facts.quote: Designed by the architectural team of Mangera Yvars and completed in 2013, the QFIS Minaretein building rests on five large columns representing the five pillars of Islam, with each featuring a verse drawn from the Qur'an.

facts.fact: The design follows the Islamic kulliyya, the idea that all knowledge comes from faith, with an endless spiral plan and paths linking classrooms to the mosque.
facts.quote: The QFIS is based on the idea of the Islamic kulliyya, suggesting that all knowledge comes from faith, explored the infinite spiral form of the building plan and the pathways which link the teaching and learning spaces to the mosque, separated symbolically  by a four-storey ablution cascade under the mosque, that helps to keep the mosque cool.

facts.fact: A four-storey ablution water cascade under the mosque helps keep it cool.
facts.quote: The QFIS is based on the idea of the Islamic kulliyya, suggesting that all knowledge comes from faith, explored the infinite spiral form of the building plan and the pathways which link the teaching and learning spaces to the mosque, separated symbolically  by a four-storey ablution cascade under the mosque, that helps to keep the mosque cool.

facts.fact: It won Best Religious Building at the 2015 World Architecture Festival and was nominated for RIBA's first international prize in 2016.
facts.quote: The building won the 2015 Best Religious Building prize at the World Architecture Festival; and in the following year it was nominated by the Royal Institute of British Architects for its inaugural international prize.

facts.fact: It has also won several sustainability awards.
facts.quote: It has also won several sustainability awards.

facts.fact: The Museum of Memory and Tolerance in Mexico City by Arditti+RDT won the World Architecture Festival's ONCE Foundation Award for Accessibility in the culture category.
facts.quote: ONCE Foundation Award for Accessibility (Category: Culture ) Museum of Memory and Tolerance in Mexico, Mexico City by Arditti+RDT/arquitectos

facts.fact: Scale Lane Footbridge is an apostrophe-shaped pedestrian swing bridge in Hull that rotates to let boats pass on the River Hull.
facts.quote: Scale Lane Footbridge is an apostrophe-shaped pedestrian swing bridge in Hull, England. The bridge has a rotating mechanism, allowing it to swing open horizontally, letting vessels pass beneath on the River Hull.

facts.fact: It was the first bridge in the world that people can stay on and ride while it moves.
facts.quote: It was the first bridge in the world to allow pedestrians to remain on the bridge and ride it while it is in motion.

facts.fact: McDowell+Benedetti won the design competition, with Alan Baxter Ltd as structural engineer; the black steel bridge opened on 28 June 2013.
facts.quote: Planning for the black steel Scale Lane Footbridge began in 2005, and McDowell+Benedetti won a competition. Alan Baxter Ltd was hired as the structural engineer on the project. The bridge officially opened on 28 June 2013.

facts.fact: It links Hull's Old Town to a former industrial area, to help regenerate it.
facts.quote: The bridge spans the river between Hull's Old Town and a former industrial section of the city. It was intended to help regeneration of the area and connect the city centre to a planned housing development.

facts.fact: The cantilevered deck curves up so small boats pass beneath, and swings open for larger ones.
facts.quote: The bridge is cantilevered and it curves upwards to allow small boats to pass beneath and swings open to allow larger boats past.

facts.fact: It weighs 1,000 tonnes, carries up to 1,000 people per crossing, and is 53 m long with a 35 m cantilever.
facts.quote: The bridge weighs 1,000 t (980 long tons; 1,100 short tons) and has a capacity of 1,000 people per crossing. It is 53 m (58 yd) long and the cantilevered portion is 35 m (38 yd) long.

facts.fact: A text and sound artwork by Nayan Kulkarni and lighting by Sutton Vane Associates signal and dramatise the bridge's movement.
facts.quote: The design includes an art installation of text and soundscape by artist Nayan Kulkarni and lighting design by Sutton Vane Associates, which also combine to signal and dramatise the bridge movement.

facts.fact: It won the World Architecture Festival transport award in 2014.
facts.quote: 2014 World Architecture Festival Transport Award (Scale Lane Bridge)

facts.fact: Sara Kulturhus in Skellefteå was designed by White Arkitekter and is listed among the notable buildings of 2021.
facts.quote: Sara Kulturhus in Skellefteå, designed by White Arkitekter.

facts.fact: The Paula Fox Melanoma and Cancer Centre is a medical centre and research institute in Melbourne.
facts.quote: The Paula Fox Melanoma and Cancer Centre is a medical centre and research institute in Melbourne, Australia.

facts.fact: Construction began on 20 June 2022 with a budget of A$152 million, half of it from state and federal government.
facts.quote: Construction of the centre began on 20 June 2022. The budget for the construction was A$152 million, with the state and federal government each contributing A$50 million.

facts.fact: Lyons Architecture designed the building's exterior to look like a skin graft.
facts.quote: The exterior of the building was designed by Lyons Architecture to look like a skin graft.

facts.fact: Kane Constructions built the project.
facts.quote: Kane Constructions delivered the project.

facts.fact: The centre was officially opened on 19 April 2024.
facts.quote: The centre was officially opened on 19 April 2024 by Victorian premier Jacinta Allan and prime minister Anthony Albanese.

facts.fact: It combines spaces for treating cancer patients with laboratories for cancer research.
facts.quote: The centre includes areas for delivering treatment to cancer patients, as well as laboratory spaces for cancer research.

facts.fact: Wyndham Court is social housing in Southampton, designed by Lyons Israel Ellis for the city council in 1966 and completed in 1969, with 184 flats, three cafés or restaurants and 13 shops.
facts.quote: It was designed by Lyons Israel Ellis for Southampton City Council in 1966, and is located near Southampton Central station and the Mayflower Theatre. Wyndham Court includes 184 flats, three cafes or restaurants and 13 shops, and was completed in 1969.

facts.fact: E. D. Lyons was the partner in charge, with Frank Linden and Aubrey Hume as architects.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architecture firm Lyons Israel Ellis, with E.D. Lyons being the partner in charge and architects Frank Linden and Aubrey Hume also assigned to the job.

facts.fact: Most of the homes are two- or three-bedroom maisonettes, with one-bedroom flats and bedsits on the first and second floors.
facts.quote: 122 of the apartments are two or three-bedroom maisonettes, with 61 one-bedroom flats and bedsits on the first and second floors, with the remaining apartment at a higher level, above the maisonettes.

facts.fact: It is built of reinforced concrete finished in white board-marked concrete, and because it sits on a hill it has six storeys at the north end and seven at the south.
facts.quote: It is built from reinforced concrete and finished with white board-marked concrete, with narrow bands painted horizontally between windows and the partition walls that separate the apartments' balconies. Because it is built on a hill, the building has six storeys at its northern end and seven at the southern.

facts.fact: Its form evokes the cruise ships that sail from Southampton, and English Heritage calls its facades sculptural and expressive.
facts.quote: Architecturally, it evokes the cruise ships which sail from the nearby port of Southampton. Its irregular facades are described by English Heritage as "sculptural and expressive".

facts.fact: The white concrete was chosen to sit well with the older civic buildings of the city centre.
facts.quote: The architects' use of white concrete was intended to be sympathetic to older civic buildings which dominate the city centre.

facts.fact: It won an Architectural Design Project award in 1966 and was Grade II listed in 1998.
facts.quote: Wyndham Court received an Architectural Design Project award in 1966 and was Grade II listed in 1998 despite opposition from the local press.

facts.fact: In 1961 the university's first vice-chancellor asked Denys Lasdun, a follower of New Brutalism, to design the permanent campus.
facts.quote: In 1961, the first vice-chancellor, Frank Thistlethwaite, had approached architect Denys Lasdun, an adherent of the "New Brutalist" trend in architecture, who was at that time building Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge, to produce designs for the permanent campus.

facts.fact: Lasdun put teaching and research in one 460-metre concrete block following the contour of the site, with a walkway along it.
facts.quote: Lasdun moved the teaching and research functions into a single 460-metre (1,510-foot) long concrete block following the contour of the site. A walkway was built alongside the teaching wall, providing access to its various entrances, with frontage roads running below.

facts.fact: Six linked blocks of terraced student rooms were attached to the walkway to read as one structure; Lasdun meant them to recall French vineyards or a rocky outcrop on a slope.
facts.quote: Attached to the southern side of the walkway, six linked blocks of terraced accommodation residences were constructed to appear as one structure. The residences became known as the "Ziggurats" and were designed by Lasdun to recall "vineyards in France or a rocky outcrop on a slope".

facts.fact: The ziggurats, in Norfolk Terrace and Suffolk Terrace, with the library and teaching wall between them, are considered one of the finest 1960s brutalist university campuses.
facts.quote: Denys Lasdun's work at the University of East Anglia, including six linked halls of residence in Norfolk Terrace and four linked halls of residence in Suffolk Terrace (commonly referred to as the 'ziggurats') and the library and 'teaching wall' between them, is considered one of the finest examples of a 1960s brutalist university campus.

facts.fact: In 1968 Bernard Feilden replaced Lasdun as consultant architect and completed the wall and library; these buildings were later listed Grade II*.
facts.quote: In 1968, Lasdun was replaced as consultant architect by Bernard Feilden, known for his conservation work on the Great Wall of China and the Taj Mahal. Feilden completed the university wall, the library, and created an arena-shaped square social space. They would later receive Grade II* listed status.

facts.fact: The ziggurats were closed in 2023 because of the RAAC concrete crisis, with no refurbishment date set as of February 2025.
facts.quote: The ziggurats were closed in 2023 as part of the reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete crisis, with no date set for their refurbishment as of February 2025.

facts.fact: The J. Edgar Hoover Building on Pennsylvania Avenue is the headquarters of the FBI.
facts.quote: The J. Edgar Hoover Building is a low-rise office building located at 935 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Washington, D.C., in the United States. It is the headquarters of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

facts.fact: Charles F. Murphy and Associates were hired in 1963, with Stanislaw Z. Gladych as chief architect.
facts.quote: In June 1963, GSA hired the firm of Charles F. Murphy and Associates to assist with the design. Stanislaw Z. Gladych was the chief architect, and Carter H. Manny, Jr. was the partner in charge.

facts.fact: Construction finished in September 1975 and President Gerald Ford dedicated it on 30 September 1975.
facts.quote: Construction finished in September 1975, and President Gerald Ford dedicated the structure on September 30, 1975.

facts.fact: It is eight storeys on Pennsylvania Avenue and 11 on E Street, with two wings joining the two main buildings around an open trapezoidal courtyard.
